tiles.title: The Spreadsheet Grid and Cell References

steps.visual_purpose: Show a small spreadsheet grid with column letters (A, B, C) and row numbers (1, 2, 3) labelled, one cell highlighted with its address called out (e.g., B2), and two visible sheet tabs at the bottom named Sheet1 and Sheet2, illustrating the full grid model in one static view.

Show a small populated grid with a rectangular block (e.g., A10:E20) highlighted in one colour and a whole-column selection (e.g., H:H) highlighted in another, so the spatial extent of each reference type is immediately visible.

Show a small Orders sheet with two amount cells (e.g. D2 and D3) and a third cell containing =D3-D2, with the formula bar visible so the learner can see the = prefix, the cell addresses, and the operator together.

Show a two-column table: the left column contains the original formula (e.g. =D2*$H$1) and the right column shows what the formula becomes after copying down several rows, with the relative part incrementing (D3, D4…) and the absolute part unchanged ($H$1), making the locking behaviour concrete.

A side-by-side view of =COUNT(C2:C51) and =COUNTA(C2:C51) applied to the same column that contains numbers, one blank cell, and one text entry, showing that COUNT returns a smaller number than COUNTA and making the distinction between the two functions immediately visible.

Show a small table with a Score column and a Grade column; the Grade column displays the nested IF formula in the formula bar and the resulting letter grades in the cells, making the branching logic and quoted text visible at a glance.

Show a spreadsheet with separate First_Name and Last_Name columns before the formula, and the resulting Full_Name column after applying TEXTJOIN, so learners can see how the delimiter and ignore_empty argument affect the combined output.

Show a small data table with two columns — raw phone numbers like '(234) 801-0000' and imported city names like ' Lagos ' — alongside a second version of the same table where a formula column displays '234' and another displays 'Lagos', making the extraction and trimming effect immediately visible.

Show a small table with a Birthdate column and an Age column side by side, with the DATEDIF/TODAY formula visible in the formula bar, so learners can see how the serial-number result of TODAY() feeds into DATEDIF as the end_date and produces a whole-number age.

Show a small sales table (Region, Date, Amount columns) alongside a results area where the SUMIFS formula is entered, so learners can see the criteria ranges highlighted and the returned total in context.

Show a two-sheet layout: a Drivers (or Products) reference table with IDs in the leftmost column and a second column of values, alongside an Orders (or Transactions) sheet where the lookup formula sits — making the left-to-right constraint of VLOOKUP and the separate-array structure of XLOOKUP immediately visible.

Show a two-column reference table with the return value (e.g. driver name) in column A and the lookup key (e.g. driver ID) in column B, making the left-of-key layout concrete and illustrating why VLOOKUP cannot be used here.

Show a small Orders-style sheet with three visible error states side by side: a VLOOKUP returning #N/A, an arithmetic formula returning #VALUE! next to a SUM over the same range returning a number, and a formula returning #REF! after its referenced column has been deleted — so learners can match each error code to its visual context.

Show the customer list table before Remove Duplicates (with visibly repeated rows highlighted) alongside the same table after (duplicate rows gone, row count reduced), so learners can see the permanent effect of the operation.

Show a single 'Full Name' column with values like 'Amara Okafor' on the left, and two separate 'First Name' / 'Last Name' columns with the split values on the right, illustrating the concrete result of the Text to Columns operation.

Show a formula bar containing a cross-sheet reference with each syntactic component — sheet name, single quotes (where required), exclamation point, and cell address — labelled with callouts, alongside a second example showing the square-bracket workbook-name syntax for a cross-workbook link.
Show the Sort dialog with two levels configured: Level 1 — Date, Oldest to Newest; Level 2 — Amount, Largest to Smallest — so learners can see that each level has its own independent Order dropdown.

Show the Orders table in three states: (1) unfiltered — all rows visible; (2) after a single column filter — a subset of rows visible with non-consecutive row numbers and a changed filter icon on that column; (3) after a second column filter is added — a smaller subset visible with changed icons on both columns.
Show a plain data range on the left and the same data as a formatted table with labeled column headers on the right, so learners can see what 'converting to a table' looks like before attempting it.

Show the Name Box containing a custom name (e.g. DeliveryTimes) while the corresponding range C2:C51 is selected, and a formula bar where the same name appears in place of the raw address, so learners can see both definition and usage in one view.

Show a completed PivotTable with callouts labelling each of the four areas — Filters (above the table), Column Labels (top), Row Labels (left), and summarized Values (body) — so learners can map the Fields pane zones to their on-sheet positions.

Show the same PivotTable side-by-side: left panel with Sum of Amount per city, right panel with Average of Amount per city, so the learner can see how the same row/column structure produces different numbers depending on the summary function.
Show a small summary table (Region | Total Sales) alongside the resulting bar chart so learners can see how the category column maps to the category axis and the numeric column maps to bar height.

Show a small time-ordered table (month column, revenue column) alongside the resulting line chart so learners can see how category data maps to the horizontal axis and value data maps to the vertical axis.

Display a finished pie chart with labelled slices showing each product category's share of total revenue, so the learner can see what a correctly encoded part-of-whole chart looks like before attempting to build one.

Show a column of numeric values before any formatting is applied, then after a Less Than rule is set — cells below the threshold appear in red, cells above remain unformatted — making the automatic, value-driven nature of the rule immediately visible.

Show the Data Validation dialog open on the Settings tab with Allow set to List and the Source box containing 'Pending,Delivered,Cancelled', alongside the resulting dropdown arrow visible in a Status column cell — illustrating the before (plain cell) and after (restricted cell with dropdown) states.
